meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of your class, and nobody called me first. Explain that.
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.
Prove it, then. Show me the document, with the times on it, and don't tell me what it means yet. And Owen doesn't cheat, so don't say that again in this room.
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.

"Eleven thirty-one at night, the night before. Two pastes, eleven fifty-two and eleven fifty-eight." I'm writing those down. Owen wrote it over the weekend, so the question is what else you have, and who saw this before the zero went into the gradebook. Also, is this the first time you've looked at his work, or the first time you've talked to me about it?
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.

"A line that doesn't exist. Which line, and where in the essay is it?" Give me the exact quote and the exact passage, and I'll check it myself. If it's made up, that's a mark you can take off. It doesn't tell me whether Owen was heard before you entered the zero, and I still want that answered.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.
I'm not defending him, I'm asking for the evidence. "He lied to you" is a conclusion, and you haven't shown me the line. Give me the quote and the passage it's in, or tell me you can't.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

No. A zero is a mark for work your own process hasn't established. Owen was never asked about the essay before you entered it, and procedure says the parent gets called before any mark consequence goes in. So you start over. Withdraw the zero, and I'll hear what supervised reassessment would look like: private, not in front of his class, with nothing placed on his record.
Ten minutes, Hale. Withdraw the zero and tell me what the reassessment looks like. If you're not ready to do that, say so, and I'll go to the principal's office next.
